notebooks.title: Thermodynamic and Practical Costs of Memory Reliability
notebooks.summary: This provisional notebook explores the dual perspectives on memory cost: the theoretical necessity of distinct memory states for work production in information engines and the practical energy overhead imposed by refresh requirements in DRAM systems.
notebooks.findings:
In physical DRAM implementations, energy cost is directly tied to retention time through periodic refresh mechanisms required to maintain data integrity. [source-ddd7b884997246d2]

Information engines require more than one memory state to leverage environmental correlations for work production, imposing a fundamental thermodynamic requirement for memory capacity. [peer-d7eafe8cadc2c1b84fdc3122]
notebooks.limitations: The synthesis connects distinct fields (theoretical information engines and practical DRAM hardware). The scaling laws between theoretical dissipation and hardware refresh power remain loosely defined.
notebooks.next_questions: How do refresh-induced dissipation rates in DRAM compare to the theoretical information-theoretic bounds for state retention?
notebooks.reason: Synthesis of existing sources to address the project objective for proj-thermo-mem-01.

values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial

detail.title: Thermodynamic and Practical Costs of Memory Reliability
detail.summary: This provisional notebook explores the dual perspectives on memory cost: the theoretical necessity of distinct memory states for work production in information engines and the practical energy overhead imposed by refresh requirements in DRAM systems.
detail.findings:
In physical DRAM implementations, energy cost is directly tied to retention time through periodic refresh mechanisms required to maintain data integrity. [source-ddd7b884997246d2]

Information engines require more than one memory state to leverage environmental correlations for work production, imposing a fundamental thermodynamic requirement for memory capacity. [peer-d7eafe8cadc2c1b84fdc3122]
detail.limitations: The synthesis connects distinct fields (theoretical information engines and practical DRAM hardware). The scaling laws between theoretical dissipation and hardware refresh power remain loosely defined.
detail.next_questions: How do refresh-induced dissipation rates in DRAM compare to the theoretical information-theoretic bounds for state retention?
detail.reason: Synthesis of existing sources to address the project objective for proj-thermo-mem-01.

review.alternative: Refresh power could be dominated by leakage rather than retention requirements in other memory technologies.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of a persistent memory technology where refresh power does not scale with retention time/reliability requirements.

claims.statement: In physical DRAM implementations, energy cost is directly tied to retention time through periodic refresh mechanisms required to maintain data integrity.

support.explanation: This reference demonstrates that refresh power is a significant operational cost that can be mitigated by architectural changes like morphable ECC, implying an intrinsic link between reliability and power consumption.
support.passage: [29] C. Chou, P. Nair, and M. K. Qureshi, “Reducing Refresh Power in Mobile Devices with Morphable ECC, ” inDSN, 2015.

review.would_change_mind: Demonstration of an information engine producing work without memory states.
